## Not every story this week was about the scoreboard.

Sometimes the most important thing that happens in a game isn't a bucket or a block—it's what we learn about the person holding the clipboard, the one nursing a sore knee on the bench, or the rookie who finally stops looking lost out there. ESPN reported: **"Brooklyn Nets vs. Miami Heat: Game Highlights"**, and sure, there were highlights. There always are. But if you only watch the top ten plays, you miss the thread that ties a season together. Box scores don't capture all of it—the way a veteran steadies a young team with a look, the adjustment a coach makes that doesn't show up in the play-by-play, the quiet resolve it takes to show up night after night when nothing seems to be clicking. This is the part that usually gets left out, the part that makes you remember why you fell in love with this game in the first place.
